question: Which of the following satellites of ISRO is an experimental satellite?
solution:
The correct answer is __**YOUTHSAT**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• YOUTHSAT is an experimental satellite of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO): 
 
• YOUTHSAT is a joint Indo-Russian mission that studies the relationship between solar variability and the thermosphere-ionosphere. 
 
• YOUTHSAT carries three payloads, two Indian and one Russian, to study the composition, energetics, and dynamics of the Earth's upper atmosphere. 
 
• YOUTHSAT launched on April 20, 2011, on the PSLV-C16/RESOURCESAT-2 launch vehicle. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• RISAT-1 (Radar Imaging Satellite)
 
 
• RISAT-1 is designed for radar imaging to provide all-weather surveillance and earth observation, especially useful for agriculture, forestry, and disaster management.
 
• It uses synthetic-aperture radar (SAR), which allows it to capture images through cloud cover and in low light, which is advantageous during the monsoon season and natural disasters.
 
• Launched on April 26, 2012.
 
• RISAT-1 is one of India’s first radar imaging satellites, enhancing the country's surveillance capabilities and contributing to various fields such as agriculture monitoring and national security.
 
 
 
• 2) RESOURCESAT-1
 
 
• RESOURCESAT-1 is dedicated to resource monitoring in India.
 
• It was designed for advanced imaging to aid in land and water resource management, including agricultural planning, forestry, and environmental monitoring.
 
• It includes cameras with different resolutions and wavelengths to capture high-quality images of Earth’s surface.
 
• Launched on October 17, 2003.
 
• Part of ISRO’s long-standing remote sensing program, RESOURCESAT-1 provided valuable data for sustainable resource management and environmental conservation efforts in India.
 
 
 
• SCATSAT-1 (Scatterometer Satellite)
 
 
• SCATSAT-1 was launched primarily for weather forecasting and climate monitoring, with a focus on sea surface wind speed and direction.
 
• This is crucial for tracking cyclones and providing early warnings for severe weather conditions.
 
• The satellite uses a scatterometer, an instrument that measures the reflection or scattering effect produced when radar waves hit the ocean surface.
 
• This helps in predicting weather changes and monitoring wind patterns over oceans.
 
• Launched on September 26, 2016.
 
• SCATSAT-1 provides vital data for weather forecasting and cyclone prediction, aiding in disaster preparedness and response.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Other experimental satellites of ISRO include:
 
• Bhaskara-I: India's first experimental remote sensing satellite, which used TV camera imagery for hydrology and forestry 
 
• Rohini Satellite RS-1: India's first indigenous satellite launch, which measured the in-flight performance of the second experimental launch of SLV-3 
 
• Rohini Technology Payload (RTP): Launched on the SLV-3E1 launch vehicle 
 
• APPLE: Launched on June 19, 1981, on the Ariane-1(V-3) launch vehicle 
 
• INS-1C: Launched on January 12, 2018, on the PSLV-C40/Cartosat-2 Series Satellite Mission
